text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 SLO breach detected for /v1/streaming/generate on shared-gpu-pool-3. p95 > 2s, p99 > 6s, elevated retry/error rates. auto-pager sent to on-call. (svc=redwood-inference, pool=shared-gpu-pool-3)

sam-sre: acked. jumping in. seeing a lot of streaming stalls reported in the traces.

anya-oncall: I'm live on it. grabbing dashboards -> latency, kernel IO, cgroup stats. tagging @raj-runtime for kernel/cgroup checks.

raj-runtime: looking. iops for /dev/nvme2 are saturated from 11:02->11:12, blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes_recursive shows repeated throttling spikes on cgroup slice for tenant:tnnt-42.

lina-mlinfra: tenant tnnt-42 had a nightly checkpoint job that started early due to retry loop. likely writes+flush pattern causing stalls.

mike-cust-succ: flagged two customers on the support queue complaining about inconsistent streaming chunks and long stalls (embedder customers). escalating.

sam-sre: can we confirm if this is noisy-tenant vs hardware fault? any SMART errors on the NVMe?

raj-runtime: no SMART faults. metrics show blkio throttling (see excerpt):

```
# from node-07
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/<container-id>/blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes_recursive
8:16 Read 0
8:16 Write 1234567890
8:16 Sync 1234567890
# timestamps align w/ spike window
```

sam-sre: that points to cgroup IO limits being hit, leading to tail latency. streaming requests block on disk writes (checkpoint KV caches).

lina-mlinfra: tenant is doing large streaming checkpoints to local NVMe. their job should be in background but apparently ran full speed.

anya-oncall: mitigation plan options: 1) throttle tnnt-42 IO weight (blkio-weight/dockerd update) 2) move tnnt-42 to dedicated node 3) add short-term capacity (bring up one extra shared node) 4) temporary routing fallback to smaller model variant for streaming customers.

sam-sre: prioritize quick actions: (A) apply soft IO throttle to the tenant container, (B) route streaming reads to cached KV replicas if possible, (C) add a new shared node if routing capacity allows.

raj-runtime: running command to reduce IO weight now:

```
# reduce blkio weight for container
docker update --blkio-weight=100 <container-id-for-tnnt-42>
# or via systemd/cgroup v1 compatibility
cgset -r blkio.weight=100 /sys/fs/cgroup/td/tnnt-42.slice
```

deploy-bot: deploy accepted, applied `docker update` on node-07, container <container-id-for-tnnt-42> now at blkio-weight=100. (deploy-bot)

anya-oncall: watching metrics. within 45s we see write throughput drop ~65% and p95 drops from 2.4s -> 400ms. p99 down to ~1.2s. streaming stalls reduced but some residual tail remains.

mike-cust-succ: notified affected customers with interim note: we are investigating a noisy background job; mitigation in progress. no data loss.

sam-sre: good. next best-effort: migrate tnnt-42 off the shared pool for the next 2 hours to avoid recurrence while we triage their job. @raj-runtime can you trigger a live migrate?

raj-runtime: starting live migration to isolated-dedicated-pool-2. command: `kubectl cordon node-07 && kubectl drain node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` then reschedule tnnt-42 pods to dedicated pool with nodeSelector:pool=dedicated-io.

lina-mlinfra: note: draining node will impact other low-priority batch tasks; we only migrate the tnnt-42 pods to avoid collateral. doing `kubectl patch` for pod tolerations now.

sam-sre: please also add a temporary routing policy to shift streaming traffic off node-07 while drain completes.

deploy-bot: routing change applied: traffic steering rule updated to deprioritize node-07 for 10m.

anya-oncall: migration finished. tnnt-42 now on dedicated-io nodes. p95 now ~230ms, p99 ~480ms. streaming stall errors dropped to baseline.

sam-sre: customer impact assessment: - duration of severe degradation window: ~11:02–11:09 (7 minutes) - partial degradation (elevated latency/retries): 11:09–11:16 (7 minutes) - impacted endpoints: /v1/streaming/generate, /v1/embeddings (shared backend) - estimated customers impacted: 4 customers saw retries, 2 had SDK-level reconnects.

mike-cust-succ: all impacted customers notified with root-cause-in-progress. we offered credits for request retries during incident window.

lina-mlinfra: follow-ups: set tenant background job QoS -> limit io burst via job scheduler, add a pre-check to avoid checkpoint spikes during high traffic windows.

raj-runtime: infra follow-ups: - add alert for per-cgroup blkio.throttle spikes (threshold > 3 spikes/min) - add automated mitigation runbook to lower blkio-weight and optionally move pod to dedicated pool - investigate using throttled io namespaces instead of coarse blkio-weight for better fairness.

sam-sre: ops follow-ups: - update SLO incident doc with precise p95/p99 numbers and timeline - run chaotic test to simulate tenant IO spikes against shared pool and measure impact - add a canary that will detect streaming stalls earlier (trace-based).

anya-oncall: handing off to @sam-sre for postmortem. i'm logging handoff now — oncall shift ends in 20m.

sam-sre: taking postmortem action items. assigning to owners in tickets. thanks @anya-oncall for the quick mitigation. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: RESOLVED: p99 SLO back within target for /v1/streaming/generate. Incident duration: 16m. Follow-up tickets created: INF-4182 (postmortem), INF-4183 (blkio alert), INF-4184 (tenant-job-qos).

mike-cust-succ: closing customer comms after PM review.

sam-sre: final note: no hardware fault. root cause = noisy tenant checkpoint job causing cgroup blkio throttling, leading to streaming stalls. primary mitigation = reduce blkio-weight + migrate to dedicated pool. long-term = scheduler/job QoS + alerts and automated mitigations.

(reacted :white_check_mark: )
